product.oneLiner: Align is a dating app played as a card game: every night you're dealt a hand of veiled cards (sky, chart, dealbreakers, no photos), and faces only flip when you both align.
oneLinerAlts: Every night you're dealt a hand of people. No photos, just their sky. (app copy, HowToPlay)
A dating app played as a card game. (BUSINESS-MODEL.md)
Read the sky before the face. (carousel core message)
product.coreLoop: deal -> deck -> align -> match -> reveal -> chat
howItWorks: Onboarding reads your chart: birth date (wheel picker), time and place, your sky, a sign reveal that flips like pulling a rare card, your big three (Sun, Moon, Rising), Venus, your element 'weather', then up to three dealbreakers that go on your card.
Your card is veiled: aura, chart and dealbreakers, no photo. Only your sun sign is ever shown to anyone; time and place never show on your card.
Every night you're dealt a deck. Each draw is six cards: five people, then a gold event card. Free gets three draws (15 people, 3 events).
Swipe right to align, left to release. Pass, and you never see who they were.
Hold a card to peek at the photo for ~3 seconds; it seals when you let go. Free gets 3 peeks a day.
Each card reads Push (where you'll rub), Pull (what draws you in) and Align (where it holds), with a strength badge from Slow burn to Rare pull. No compatibility score, by design.
If you both align, it's a match: the auras collide, 'You both aligned', then the cards flip and the veil lifts off the photo.
Chat opens from something on their card ('Say the honest thing'). Chats fade if nobody talks ('Seven days to speak').
In chat you play talk cards (both answer, neither shows until both have) and place cards (pick a place and a night; if they say yes, it's a date; check in at partner venues for an exclusive card).
After 3 days aligned you can trade copies of your cards into each other's binder.
A new deal lands at 11:11 every night.

rules: BRAND-QA: Plain and practical. Short sentences. Sentence case for body, uppercase only in mono eyebrows. No jargon, no exclamation-heavy hype.
BRAND-QA: Buttons say what happens ("Open packs", "Play it to Juniper").
Carousel: Lowercase. Blunt, warm and a little funny. A friend who is done watching you text them first.
Carousel: Short words. No hashtag-speak, no emoji in slides, no exclamation marks, no "bestie", no "manifest", no therapy jargon ("attachment style" etc.).
Carousel: Astrology is the lens, not a lecture: name the sign and one true trait, then give advice that would be right for anyone.
Carousel: It can sting, but it never punches down at a sign or a person. The target is the behaviour.
Carousel: Never promise a soulmate or claim astrology decides anything. Align says "read".
Carousel: Align's core message is sprinkled in subtly: never an ad, never "download Align". At most two Align vocabulary words per piece.
Reels: Calm, warm and honest, like a letter written at 2am by someone who knows you. Reflective rather than blunt; it can still sting a little.
Reels: No emoji, no hashtags in lines, no exclamation marks, no "manifest", no therapy jargon, no promises of a soulmate. Astrology "reads", it never decides.
Reels: Align's ideas are slipped in at most twice, never sold, never "download".
Original only: never reuse another creator's footage, narration, lines or audio.
banned: punching down at a sign or person
compatibility score / percent match framing (the product has none by design)
reusing other creators' footage, lines or audio
visual: gold buttons/pills/badges, pure black or grey surfaces, pure white text

audience.who: Single, astrology-curious daters (onboarding blocks under-18s; seeded profiles are mid-20s to ~30) who are tired of photo-first swiping; launching in Houston. Secondary: collectors and couples (talk decks sold to couples, cards kept after the app is cancelled).
pains: Being judged by a photo first
Swiping endlessly with nothing real said
Learning the dealbreakers (kids, money, how you fight) on date five instead of up front
Opening lines that are cute instead of true
Compatibility scores that pretend to decide for you
Dating apps you delete the moment they work
desires: To be read for who they are (their sky, their words) before their face
Something honest and lasting ('Wants something that lasts')
Dating that feels like play: decks, pulls, rare cards, packs
Something to keep and collect, online and in real life
Not arriving alone: people near them who match their sky
